body.en: Autogamy is *pollination* within the same flower; cleistogamous flowers such as Viola, Oxalis and Commelina never open and are always autogamous. Geitonogamy is transfer to another flower of the same plant: genetically it is self-pollination. Xenogamy brings genetically different pollen from another plant. Wind-pollinated flowers have light, non-sticky pollen and feathery stigmas (maize tassels). Water pollination occurs in Vallisneria, Hydrilla and the marine seagrass Zostera. Most flowers use animals, and offer nectar and pollen as rewards.
body.kn: ಸ್ವಪರಾಗಸ್ಪರ್ಶ (ಆಟೋಗಮಿ) ಅದೇ ಹೂವಿನಲ್ಲಿ, ಗೈಟೋನೋಗಮಿ ಅದೇ ಸಸ್ಯದ ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಹೂವಿನಲ್ಲಿ, ಪರಪರಾಗಸ್ಪರ್ಶ (ಕ್ಸೀನೋಗಮಿ) ಬೇರೆ ಸಸ್ಯದ ಹೂವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಗಾಳಿ, ನೀರು ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಳು ಪರಾಗಸ್ಪರ್ಶಕಗಳು.

title.en: Board: kinds and agents of pollination

say.en: Pollination can be within the same flower, autogamy; to another flower of the same plant, geitonogamy; or to a flower of another plant, xenogamy.
Agents: wind needs light, dry pollen and feathery stigmas; water pollinates Vallisneria, Hydrilla and Zostera; most flowers use animals and offer nectar and pollen.
Plants avoid self-pollination in four ways. Monoecious castor and maize stop autogamy only; dioecious papaya stops both autogamy and geitonogamy.
On a compatible stigma the pollen germinates; the pollen tube grows down the style and enters the ovule through the micropyle, guided by the filiform apparatus.

explanation.en: Wind-pollinated flowers have light, non-sticky pollen, well-exposed stamens, large feathery stigmas and often a single ovule (maize, grasses). Water pollination happens in Vallisneria, Hydrilla and the seagrass Zostera, whose long ribbon-like pollen is carried inside the water. Animal-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar, with sticky pollen (Amorphophallus, Yucca and its moth).

body.en: Continued self-pollination causes inbreeding depression, so plants prevent it: *pollen* release and stigma receptivity are not synchronised, anther and stigma sit at different positions, self-incompatibility blocks self-pollen, and unisexual flowers are produced. Castor and maize (monoecious) prevent autogamy but not geitonogamy; papaya (dioecious) prevents both. The pistil recognises compatible pollen: the pollen tube grows through the style and enters the ovule, usually through the micropyle, guided by the filiform apparatus.
body.kn: ಸತತ ಸ್ವಪರಾಗಸ್ಪರ್ಶ ಅಂತರ್ಸಂಕರ ಕುಸಿತಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣ. ಸ್ವ-ಅಸಾಮರಸ್ಯ, ಏಕಲಿಂಗಿ ಹೂಗಳು ಮುಂತಾದ ಉಪಾಯಗಳು ಇದನ್ನು ತಡೆಯುತ್ತವೆ. ಶಲಾಕೆ ಸರಿಯಾದ ಪರಾಗವನ್ನು ಗುರುತಿಸಿ ಪರಾಗನಳಿಕೆ ಬೆಳೆಯಲು ಬಿಡುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Wind: light, non-sticky pollen; well-exposed stamens; large, often feathery stigmas; often a single ovule per ovary; many flowers in an inflorescence. Water: rare, about 30 genera, mostly monocots.

Bees, butterflies, flies, beetles, wasps, ants, moths, birds (sunbirds, hummingbirds), bats, and even some primates and reptiles pollinate. Insect-pollinated flowers are usually large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar; small flowers cluster into an inflorescence.

Choose parents with the desired characters (e.g. a high-yield and a disease-resistant wheat). Emasculation: remove the anthers from the female parent's bisexual flower bud with forceps before they dehisce.

question.en: Which pollination type is functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to self-pollination?

explain.en: Geitonogamy needs a pollinating agent, but the pollen comes from the same plant.

takeaway.en: Autogamy, geitonogamy (same plant), xenogamy (different plant; only one giving new genes).

problem.en: In an artificial hybridisation programme with a bisexual flower, list the steps in order.

steps.en: Remove the anthers from the flower bud before they dehisce: this is emasculation.
Cover the emasculated flower with a bag of butter paper to keep out unwanted pollen.
When the stigma is receptive, dust it with pollen collected from the chosen male parent.
Rebag the flower and let the fruit develop.

answer.en: Emasculation → bagging → pollination with chosen pollen → rebagging
